title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Motion Study. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show composition and palette only; text renders as bars.

options.label: Motion Study
options.lineage: Frank & Lillian Gilbreth's 1910s light-trace motion studies and flow process charts
options.thesis: Every project shown as a time-and-motion study: the wasted path, then the improved one.
options.viewport: A long-exposure plate fills the screen: a tangled light trace of a manual process resolving into one clean line, with name, hook, Download CV and Contact set on the plate.
options.risk: A dark photographic hero edges toward the dark-with-glow default, so it must read as silver photography, not neon; each case study needs real before/after step counts.

raised.raise: Traces have a lifecycle: the wasted 'before' path fades to an afterimage as the improved path draws, so history stays visible without clutter.
The trace plate owns the first viewport at monumental scale and crops on phones instead of shrinking.
System states print themselves: contact-form sending, sent and error appear as entries on the process chart, not toasts.
Step colours are law: each colour means exactly one kind of step (operation, transport, delay, inspection) and never decorates.
Arriving at a section marks it in the nav with its process-chart symbol, so the page shows where you are in the flow.

options.label: Network Diagram
options.lineage: Beck and Vignelli-style transit diagrams; Melbourne's train network map
options.thesis: Your systems drawn as a transit map: payroll, Xero, Reckon and Cloudflare as stations, integrations as lines.
options.viewport: A full-width network map where each line is an integration and each interchange a project; name and actions sit in the map's legend panel.
options.risk: Integrations-as-metro-lines is a familiar portfolio trope, and it shows wiring better than it shows improvement.

options.label: Folded CV
options.thesis: A one-page CV packet that deploys into the full field of case studies with one pull.
options.viewport: A compact CV packet at centre; one pull unfolds it into a crease grid where each cell is a project.
options.case: Fuses well for recruiters, who already hold a CV, but it shows breadth rather than automation and improvement. It holds the audience axis only.
options.risk: The fold mechanic can slow a skim on phones; it needs stepped deployment there.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: The cursor draws glowing wakes across a dark sea.
options.viewport: A dark field where pointer trails glow and fade.
options.case: Loses both axes: recruiters don't identify with it, and it says nothing about improvement.
options.kept: Traces with a lifecycle: excited, radiant, fading.

options.label: Woodcut Identity
options.thesis: Warm woodcut marks stamped over torn kraft paper.
options.viewport: A stamped woodcut mark over torn paper strips.
options.case: Loses both axes: off-register for an engineering hire and unrelated to automation.
options.kept: A mark stamped per section to show progress.

options.label: Linocut Broadside
options.thesis: Monumental gouged figures with carved demand lettering.
options.viewport: One figure filling the sheet from below, carved headline.
options.case: Loses both axes: protest register misfits a job search.
options.kept: Monumental scale that crops rather than shrinks.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as one live terminal transcript.
options.viewport: An 80-column transcript with a breathing cursor.
options.case: Loses both axes: the developer-portfolio cliché, and opaque to recruiters.
options.kept: System states print themselves instead of appearing as chrome.

options.label: Arcade Cabinet
options.thesis: The career as a pixel-art game screen.
options.viewport: A tile-grid stage with a score bar.
options.case: Loses both axes: gamified novelty undercuts a serious hire.
options.kept: Palette law: each colour reserved for one meaning.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, light developer portfolio executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Hero with name and role, metrics row, project cards, experience timeline.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other candidates by design.
